notes.decision: Translated 'the first standing-fast' preserving the verbal-spatial nominalization of ⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ 'stand fast,' attested in glossary as a substantival cosmic title (cf. ⲡⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧϩ 'the standing-fast / the establishment'). The Father is here identified as the foundational standing — first in a series presumably continued through the Living Spirit and other emanations.

Rendered 'the petition.' The form is unusual; in context (governed by relative ⲉⲧⲁⲥⲥⲁⲡⲥⲧ̄ 'which she had supplicated him for') it functions as the cognate object of ⲥⲱⲡⲥ̄ 'petition.' Possibly a Lycopolitan substantival form of ⲥⲱⲡⲥ̄, or alternatively cognate with ⲥⲟⲉⲓⲧ 'cry, report.' Confidence moderate.

Translated 'the first Expander.' Compound: ⲣⲉϥ- ('one who does') + ϯ ('give') + ⲟⲩⲁⲥⲧⲛ̄ ('expanse, breadth' — cf. accumulated ⲟⲩⲉⲥⲧⲁⲛⲧ 'wide/broad'). Standard agentive formation paralleling ⲣⲉϩ†ⲥⲃⲱ 'teacher.' The epithet is confirmed by line 28-29 ⲁϩϯⲟⲩⲁⲥⲧⲛ̄ ⲛⲉϩ ⲍⲛ̄ ⲧⲭⲱⲣⲁ ⲙ̄ⲡⲙ̄ⲧⲁⲛ 'and gave him expanse in the country of rest' — the Living Spirit's defining cosmic act. 'Expander' preserves the active verbal-emission semantics required by the correspondential principle.

Translated 'struck him down.' The verb is from the same root as accumulated ⲃⲁⲡϩ 'to be struck down/defeated' (used of the dark powers' defeat). Here in active form with 3sg.m suffix; the object 'him' must refer to the dark adversary that had weakened the First Man (referenced by ⲛ̄ⲧⲁϩⲣ̄ⲃⲱⲃ 'because he had been weakened' immediately preceding). The sequence then continues with the Living Spirit's rescue of the First Man (took him in, released him, set him on his feet, gave him expanse).

Rendered 'a binding.' In context the First Man finds himself 'in the midst of the encampment of demons, a ⲧⲱⲃϥ̄ of the powers of the Devil' — in apposition with the previous loci of imprisonment. Most plausibly from ⲧⲱⲃⲉ 'seal, bind' with 3sg.m suffix, hence 'a sealing/binding of him by the powers of the Devil.' Distinct from the homograph ⲧⲱⲃⲍ̄ 'pray' used elsewhere on the page. Confidence moderate.

Translated 'and he joined himself to the Mother of Life.' ⲧⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲁϩ likely a Lycopolitan reflex of ⲧⲟⲩⲱϩ 'add, join, attach.' The First Man's pre-cosmic conjunction with the Mother of Life (before his descent) is a standard Manichaean cosmogonic moment.

This kephalaion appears to recapitulate the cosmogonic narrative of the First Man's rescue — the Mother of Life's intercessory prayer, the Father's response, the Living Spirit's descent, and the rescue from the Deep — in preparation for an enumeration of the cosmic 'standing-fasts' (Father = first; Living Spirit = (third?), apparently associated with the ὑποδοχεύς 'receiver' in line 31). The damaged final lines suggest a typology comparing emanations.
